Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: Pick A. It closes the hole using data the workflow already has, with one `/user` read. The vulnerable branch is the `closed_unmerged` arm at `.github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:555-556`. Today it closes every issue that `extract_repo_scoped_issue_refs_from_text` or the closing references pull out of a same-repository PR (lines 360-381). Requiring all three of a same-repository head, an exact `ai/issue-<n>` head branch, and a PR author equal to the `GH_PAT` account stops an outside PR author from closing unrelated issues. Pipeline-created implementation PRs still close as before when they are abandoned.

B is rejected because anyone who can push to the repository can create an `ai/issue-<n>` branch, so it is not a real binding. C would stop closing the issues of every PR opened before the change and adds a new marker contract. D changes behaviour that the stall and unblock machinery and the `ai:closed` lineage rely on.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
(Not required: Q1 is a lettered decision. The implementation notes below are the binding interpretation of A.)
Q1:
  inputs:
    - `.github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml`, step "Update linked issue labels when PR closes" (env at lines 190-200, branch-issue parse at line 374, completion check at lines 554-571).
  steps:
    - Add to that step's `env:` `PR_HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}` and `PR_AUTHOR_LOGIN: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}`. These come from the event payload, so they cost no API call.
    - Only when `PR_MERGED != true`, resolve the `GH_PAT` login once with `gh_retry gh api user --jq .login`. Cache it for the loop and fail closed if it is empty or the call errors.
    - In the `PR_MERGED != true` arm, set `target_merge_reason=closed_unmerged` only when all four hold:
      - `PR_HEAD_REPO == REPOSITORY`;
      - `BRANCH_ISSUE_NUMBER == issue_number`, using the existing anchored `^ai/issue-([0-9]+)([-/].*)?$` parse;
      - the login was resolved;
      - `PR_AUTHOR_LOGIN` equals it.
    - For every other issue on an unmerged close, `continue` before line 571. The issue's labels and state stay unchanged and it is not added to `LINEAGE_FINALIZE_ISSUE_NUMBERS`. Log the skip with a fixed reason token (`unbound_issue`, `foreign_head`, `author_mismatch` or `identity_unavailable`) and the issue/PR numbers, without printing PR text.
    - Leave the merged-PR arms (lines 557-565) exactly as they are. Tracking-issue skipping (lines 531-534) also stays as is.
    - Add a contract test covering: a bound pipeline PR is closed; an unrelated referenced issue on an unmerged close is untouched; a non-pipeline author is rejected; a fork or other-repo head is rejected; an unavailable identity is rejected. Each rejected issue must also be kept out of lineage finalization.
    - Write a changelog fragment under `changelog.d/`. Write an `agents.d/` fragment that states the new unmerged-close binding rule.
  reversibility: Changing a single predicate in the workflow restores the old behaviour. Issues this change leaves open are still covered by the poller's stall and unblock sweeps, so a wrong skip only delays a close.

The question shows a single lettered decision (A), so no ESCALATION or SETUP REQUIRED section applies.
